report.summary: Chunk 2 of worktree.py: defines WorktreeRemovalRace, _worktree_root_for, _lexical, _key, _is_within, _is_reparse_point, _path_identity; includes docstrings and comments with claims about behaviour.
risks: _worktree_root_for | medium | Uses env var DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT; if set to a symlink, _lexical is not used to resolve it before containment checks. | Check if caller applies _lexical to the root before use.

_is_reparse_point | high | getattr(st, 'st_reparse_tag', 0) may not exist on all platforms; docstring claims it is absent on Linux/macOS, but code still calls it. If attribute is missing, getattr returns 0 and function returns False, meaning symlinks on those platforms are NOT detected by this branch, only by the S_ISLNK/islink branch. The docstring acknowledges this but the risk is that if a future Python version adds the attribute for non-reparse files, the belt-and-braces check could return false positives.

_is_reparse_point | medium | On Windows, st_file_attributes may not include FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT for all reparse points (e.g., some third-party ones). The belt-and-braces check on st_reparse_tag catches those, but if st_reparse_tag is not populated (e.g., on some filesystems), reparse points may be missed.

_path_identity | low | Docstring claims lstat populates st_dev and st_ino for a directory on Windows 11, CPython 3.10.11. This is platform-specific and may not hold on other Windows versions or Python builds.

handoff.purpose: Define worktree exception, root resolution, lexical path utilities, reparse detection, and path identity function.

symbols.name: WorktreeRemovalRace
symbols.note: Exception raised when a reparse point appears above an ongoing removal. Inherits from WorktreeContainmentError.

symbols.name: _worktree_root_for
symbols.note: Resolves the root directory for candidate worktrees based on env var or platform defaults. Returns a Path.

symbols.name: _lexical
symbols.note: Returns absolute-and-normalised path without touching filesystem (no symlink resolution).

symbols.name: _key
symbols.note: Returns a case-folded, normalised string for comparison.

symbols.name: _is_within
symbols.note: Lexically checks if child path is parent or under it.

symbols.name: _is_reparse_point
symbols.note: Returns True if path is a symlink, junction, mount point, or any reparse point (via lstat attributes).

symbols.name: _path_identity
symbols.note: Returns (st_dev, st_ino) from lstat, or None if path does not exist.

claims.text: Distinct from every other containment refusal, and the distinction is the whole point: the others mean "nothing was removed", this one means "the walk stopped partway, on purpose".
claims.why: The claim refers to other containment refusal classes not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Worktrees must live OUTSIDE the primary checkout so they never pollute git status or whole-repo snapshot attribution.
claims.why: The claim about git status and snapshot attribution is not verifiable from this code alone.

claims.text: DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT env override (still namespaced per repo).
claims.why: Code checks os.environ.get('DAEDALUS_WORKTREE_ROOT') and uses it as base if set.
Code uses Path(local_appdata) / 'daedalus' / 'worktrees' when LOCALAPPDATA is set.
Code uses Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / 'daedalus' / 'worktrees' when LOCALAPPDATA is unset.

claims.text: Each repo gets its own subdirectory keyed by a short digest of the resolved repo path so distinct checkouts never collide.
claims.why: The claim about digest being of the resolved repo path is not verifiable because the input repo_path may not be resolved; the code uses str(repo_path) directly.

claims.text: os.path.normpath collapses .. textually; unlike resolve() it cannot be redirected by a symlink, which is exactly the property needed before a containment decision.
claims.why: The function uses os.path.normpath and os.path.abspath, which are lexical operations and do not follow symlinks.

claims.text: Comparison form: case-folded on Windows, normalised everywhere.
claims.why: Function uses os.path.normcase (case-folding on Windows) and os.path.normpath.

claims.text: True if child is parent or lies under it, lexically.
claims.why: Function checks if key(child) == key(parent) or starts with parent + separator.

claims.text: os.path.islink is NOT sufficient on Windows: a junction created with mklink /J has reparse tag IO_REPARSE_TAG_MOUNT_POINT, not ...SYMLINK, so islink returns False for it (measured on this machine).
claims.why: The claim about islink returning false for junctions is based on a measurement not present in this code.

claims.text: The FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT bit on lstat catches every reparse kind, including tags that do not exist yet.
claims.why: Code checks attrs & FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT; this bit is set for all reparse points.

claims.text: THE FIRST LINE IS THE ONLY ONE THAT EXISTS OFF WINDOWS, and it is worth saying because the two Windows-specific answers below it are what the junction tests exercise. st_file_attributes and st_reparse_tag are not members of a stat_result on Linux/macOS at all, so on those platforms both getattr calls yield the default and deleting the S_ISLNK/islink line turns this whole function into return False -- every symlink followed, every guard in this file silently open.
claims.why: The code uses getattr with default 0, which on platforms without those attributes returns 0. The function then returns False from the belt-and-braces check. The first line (S_ISLNK/islink) remains the only detection on non-Windows.

claims.text: That mutation SURVIVED the suite until 2026-07-28; it is killed now by test_reparse_detection_off_windows_rests_on_the_symlink_branch, which simulates the POSIX stat SHAPE rather than skipping off Windows.
claims.why: The referenced test is not in this chunk.

claims.text: NO-FOLLOW, and that is the whole point. It reads os.lstat, not os.stat.
claims.why: The code uses os.lstat (not os.stat) to get identity without following symlinks.

claims.text: An earlier version used os.stat, which FOLLOWS a reparse point, and that made the identity FORGEABLE by the one primitive this module exists to defend against -- measured on this box, against the manager's own repo_path: ...
claims.why: The measurement results and the earlier version are not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Measured on this box (Windows 11, CPython 3.10.11): lstat populates both fields for a DIRECTORY, os.rename PRESERVES them (same NTFS record
claims.why: The claim about os.rename preserving inode is not verifiable from this code; the measurement is not in this chunk.

observations.what: _worktree_root_for uses str(repo_path) directly without resolving symlinks; the docstring says 'resolved repo path' but the code does not resolve.

_is_reparse_point uses getattr with default 0 for st_file_attributes and st_reparse_tag; on platforms where these attributes exist but are 0 for a symlink, the function would return True from the S_ISLNK branch anyway, but if that branch is removed, it would return False.
_path_identity function is defined but the code chunk ends before the function body completes; the docstring claim about os.rename preserving inode is not verifiable.
